Organise defects before scheduling access.

We begin with the relevant building areas and the scope approved by your representative. Entry doors, corridors, external surfaces and water-related defects are recorded by location. This gives the property team a clear basis for decisions, resident coordination and staged completion.

01 / Access control at an entrance

Work across the shared property

On a common-area list, keep the address, level, side and defect number on each row. Identify which issues need a committee decision, a lot owner’s access or a manager’s approval. Check the applicable plan and agreed work boundary before combining a private defect with corridor repairs.

  • Doors, corridors and amenities

    We scope door hardware, wall and ceiling damage, fixed fittings and agreed amenity repairs. Each item identifies the part affected and the finish or operation to be restored.

  • Building and outdoor areas

    Reported roof, balcony, façade, paving and drainage issues are separated by building element. Access above, below and through occupied areas is recorded with the defect.

Fire, security & access ↗
02 / Shared property entry and finishes

Confirm the element and the boundary

Queensland maintenance responsibilities depend on the scheme and relevant boundaries. We use the property information supplied by your representative when defining the work, including whether the item sits within the approved common-property scope.

A repair, an investigation and an upgrade are different decisions. We keep them visible in the scope, so a leaking area is not automatically priced as a full replacement and a requested upgrade is not buried inside routine maintenance.

Fire, security & access ↗

Coordinate access before attendance

For several defects along a shared corridor, match each item to its location and approved scope. Agree the route residents will use during the work and who verifies the area before barriers are removed.

  1. 01

    Group the work

    We group related defects while retaining individual location references. Repeated hardware or finish requirements can then be checked together.

  2. 02

    Agree the occupied-area plan

    Your representative coordinates resident notices and access permissions. We identify work zones, material movement and any temporary change to normal routes.

  3. 03

    Record changes

    If opened-up areas reveal additional work, we record the finding and seek the nominated decision before adding that scope.

Entry
  1. Confirm approval
  2. Keep a route open
  3. Check door and finishes
Outdoor common areas
  1. Confirm boundaries
  2. Work in zones
  3. Reopen to residents

What shapes the scope and quote

  • Material matching

    Existing hardware, coatings, surface profiles and any retained components determine the repair detail and replacement options.

  • Access and extent

    Height, resident access, the number of affected areas, investigation and staged attendances are identified separately where relevant.

Close out against the approved list.

We keep completed work and matters awaiting a resident, manager or committee decision against the same location numbers.

Close out by location

Match completion notes and photos to the approved defect list. Record parts orders and follow-up checks separately.

A location written as level, entry and element is easier to verify than a general request for the building. We match each item to the approved common-area scope, record who provides access and preserve a route past work where residents still need to use the building.

  • Numbered locations and marked plan
  • Approval and notice contact
  • Open items by location

Common questions

Common questions

Can we start with photographs and a committee defect list?+

Yes. Label the location and describe the symptom for each item. We use the list to identify defined repairs and areas that need inspection before the final scope is agreed.

Can repairs be split across several stages?+

We can group the approved work by building, level or access window. Each stage needs a clear boundary, completion record and any conditions affecting the next stage.

Can we include an issue inside a lot on the same list?+

Record it separately and confirm who approves the investigation or repair using the property plan and relevant arrangements.
